paragraphs: Tzurba me-rabbanan. Rashi, Ta'anit 4a, explains: distinguished. This term is used for young pupils, whereas of elders one says ‘one of the rabbis.’ This is not so, for in Mi She-Meto, 19a, Rav Pappa said concerning Mar Shmuel (see the Gemara: in Ein Yaakov the reading is different; see Mar Shmuel, for both here and in Ein Yaakov there is an error): ‘A Torah scholar is different, for the Holy One, blessed be He, demands his honor.’ In Ha-Sholeah Get (and in Kol Kitvei and in Mo’ed Katan 26b:24), Rava called Abba bar Minyomi, who was old, a tzurba me-rabbanan (see there). In Ha-Mappelet, 24b, Abaye said concerning R' Yehoshua ben Hangeya, who was very old: ‘A Torah scholar who says something should state its reason,’ etc. (see Hananya, R' Yehoshua's brother). Rather, one who has read Scripture, studied Mishnah, and served in Torah study [שימש ת״ת; wording requires collation]—that is, Talmud—is a tzurba me-rabbanan, like Rav Menashya bar Tahlifa (see there), Sheloshah She-Akhelu, 47b. In Beitzah 20b: a scholar whose colleague says something to him should not answer him more than he said. In Nedarim 62a:10 and 62a:12: a scholar may say, ‘Settle my case first,’ and may identify himself where people do not know him. In Shabbat 119, beginning of a, Mar bar Rav Ashi said: ‘I am disqualified from judging a Torah scholar, because he is as dear to me as my own self.’ Rava said there: ‘May I receive reward for this: when a Torah scholar comes before me for judgment, I do not lay my head upon the pillow until I have examined the arguments in his favor.’
